description:
FOUND s499 (Fable, 2026-09-27) by the s496a merge-review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/review/f-Q-string.pl; out/f-Q-string.{perl,base,tree}.out).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 1b0baa7c and on the s496a tree 0ab64a45; nothing to do with regexes -- it is string interpolation.

THE TABLE (perl 5.40.3 -> PCL), each a double-quoted string:
    "\Q\pM\E"   perl  \Q\pM\E        PCL  \pM        (`\` is an escaped backslash; the Q/p/E are plain letters)
    "x\Qy]: "     perl  x\Qy]:         PCL  x\y\]\:\    (the false \Q runs to the end of the string and quotemetas everything after it)
    "\Q"          perl  \Q             PCL  \ then the rest of the print LIST mangled
    "\Qa.b"       perl  \Qa.b          PCL  a\.b
    "\U\Lx"      perl  \U\Lx          PCL  x
    "\Uab"        perl  \Uab           PCL  AB          <-- "C:\Users\Eve" is this row: a Windows path in an ordinary script
    "\Q\x\E"      perl  \x            PCL  \x   (right)
    "\Qa.b\E" / "\Uab\E" / "\Q$v\E"     right on both
  Single-quoted strings are unaffected.  In a REGEX literal the probe row agrees with perl (`/\Q\pM\E/`), so the regex path scans the source text; the string path does not.

WHERE: the double-quoted string escape processing in Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm (`unescape_string` ~line 701 and the delimiter/escape helpers ~343) versus the case-modifier (`\Q \U \L \u \l \E`) scan -- the modifier scan must see the SOURCE text where `\` is ONE token (an escaped backslash) and never re-read the character after it as an escape.  Rule 11: the regex path already does this right -- find its scanner (Pl/InterpScan.pm is the ONE interpolation scanner, standing rule Â§8) and route the string path through the same tokenization instead of a second pass over unescaped text.
FIX + BAR: Pl/ emission change (gen bump), corpus-diff read per file (strings with `\Q`/`\U`/`\L`/`\E` are the only expected movers -- grep the corpus for them first to know the population), guard rows in an existing string-interpolation Pl/t file (the table above; inverse-verified), the full sweep (op/quotemeta.t, op/lc.t, base/lex.t carry these shapes).
PRIORITY: HIGH among correctness fillers -- a Windows path or a LaTeX/regex snippet in a double-quoted string is ordinary code, and the failure is SILENT (rule 12 family); estimated <= 1 h at the right layer.
=== DONE (s499h) ===
ExprToCL::_apply_case_escapes decodes a dq literal's SOURCE in ONE scan (each \X one unit; the case escapes are commands, never markers in decoded text).  Also perl's toke.c stack rule in BOTH dq scans (literal + StringInterpolation): a new \U \L \F closes open U/L/F groups (and a \Q above) first; \E pops one.  Probes p1 (29 rows: plain dq, qq{}, heredoc, s/// replacement, string eval, breaking cases) + p5 (18) = perl except p1 row 28 ("\U\x{e9}", #2092 family).  corpus-diff vs 61571685: oct.t only ("0\L$1%\U$1" now 0b%B as perl); emission-ab lib 29 SAME; ir-host-leak identical.  Guard Pl/t/case-invert-01.t rows 19-22, inverse-verified.  Gate 269/9025 PASS, sweep TOTAL 18714 (+0) GATE clean, EVERYDAY 102 of 122 unchanged.  ir-spec Â§3.2g.  Residue: #2470 (backslash-newline).  gen v2-2780.
subject: SILENT WRONG in ordinary strings: the `\Q \U \L \E` (case/quote modifier) scan of a double-quoted string runs on the ESCAPE-PROCESSED text, so an escaped backslash followed by Q/U/L/E is taken as the modifier -- "C:\Users" prints "C:SERS", "\Qa.b" prints "a\.b", "x\Qy]: " swallows the rest of the string
